headline: Disney plans to pay $60 million a year to hire 66 employees of the bankrupt chatbot company Character.AI, according to a bankruptcy filing.
score_reason: Follow-up with new figures from a court filing on a deal we already covered; interesting for AI talent pay but limited in scale.
importance_line: Disney is paying heavily for AI talent after laying off several hundred of its own workers, which matters to its employees and shareholders, but the figures come from a court filing, Disney did not respond to requests for comment, and an entertainment lawyer told Business Insider such pay is "not that unusual in this space".
summary: Business Insider reports, citing a bankruptcy filing by Character.AI's parent company, that Disney plans to pay $60 million a year to 66 Character.AI employees, with a further $30 million set aside to keep them, and expects to spend $180 million on their pay and retention over three years. This is new since our 14 Oct 2026 report that Disney would pay $20 million for some of Character.AI's assets: 56 of the 66 have already left Character.AI, the other 10 await visa updates, and rival bidders have until 20 November to offer for the assets under a bankruptcy judge's oversight.
notes: Read in full. The filing is dated Tuesday (read as 13 Oct 2026); the pay figures are new compared with our 14 Oct item. Score kept at 5 because the figures are new to our readers.
